answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 11 for every participant already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. The zenith multiplier is published, charged in sonnet, and ledge lists each payment. A burst of registrations as a result prices itself out, since the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 2830 identities would post 3779 proofs and burn roughly 12 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
